page: Amazon Web Services c8i.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 480 MB L3 cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

This instance does not include local storage and relies on network-attached storage, with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. It does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2175.0 and strong single-threaded compression speeds, including 34.3 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.34 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations are more limited, as evidenced by a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2747.0 and a poor stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 2158.29. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 22.25 GB/sec for large block read-only operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i.large offers a modern DDR5 memory architecture and dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources at a low entry point within the Gen8 family, though it is constrained by its 2 vCPU limit and 4.0 GB RAM capacity. This resource density makes it suitable for single-threaded tasks, lightweight text processing, and basic web serving. It is also appropriate for small-scale development, testing, or running lightweight utility services that benefit from high single-core clock speeds but do not require extensive multi-core scaling or large memory footprints.
